metric: planBefore/planAfter pairs from Calcite's current rule tests, translated to SQL, proved equivalent; 1 genuine Calcite non-equivalence refuted with a DuckDB counterexample, 128 unknown. 86 of the 168 pairs new to every other corpus are proved.
caveats: Calcite commit 2d28ce3 (2026-09-30). 502 of 1016 tests translate exactly; 182 leave the plan unchanged (not rewrites) and 332 are skipped with reasons (tests/fixtures/calcite_mined/skipped.jsonl). 334 of the 502 overlap SQLSolver, QED or R-Bot, whose pairs rules were developed against (tuned on test); the 168 new pairs were not used for development. While building the ANY/ALL rules, 7 held-out pairs were read (testJoinConditionOrExpansionRuleAnti, testNullSelect2, testSomeWithGreaterThanNoRowSubQuery, testSomeWithLessThanOrEqualNoRowSubQuery, testTopDownGeneralDecorrelateForFilterSome, testTopDownGeneralDecorrelateForSubqueryWithJoin, testNotInNullableKey); 2 of them are proved, so 61 of the 63 held-out proofs are clean.
correctness: 0 false proofs; every proof and refutation re-run on 60 random DuckDB databases, half skewed towards the literals
held_out: 86/168 on pairs new to every other corpus, tuned on test: they scored 53/168 before any rule was developed against them; the set-operation rules were written with their unknowns in view, and 7 were read while building the ANY/ALL rules (quantified_rules.py). Rules since then were developed on the other 334 pairs and QED only; they lifted the new pairs from 76 to 78. The cast and constant rules (cast_rules.py) were developed with two held-out pairs in view, testProjectAggregateMergeSum01 and testUnionToValuesByUnionAll3; both now prove, and they lifted the new pairs from 78 to 80. The outer-join flattening rules (outer_join_flatten.py) lifted them from 80 to 86; all 6 gained pairs were among the failing pairs read in the 2026-10-02 triage, so they are not clean.
